verdict.rationale: The Messages API documents incremental token streaming via SSE with `"stream": true`, and the SDKs ship built-in streaming support, including fine-grained tool-input streaming. Latency behavior is documented through several levers: fast mode gives up to 2.5x output speed, the effort parameter trades intelligence for latency, and prompt caching cuts latency. missing for 10: concrete published latency figures (time-to-first-token or sub-second full-answer guarantees), independent or hands-on latency corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream responses token by token (or get sub-second full answers) with the latency behavior documented

citations.quote: When creating a Message, you can set "stream": true to incrementally stream the response using server-sent events (SSE)
built-in support for streaming, retries, and error handling
Fine-grained tool streaming delivers a tool's input to your client as Claude generates it, without server-side buffering or JSON validation.
support fast mode (research preview), which delivers up to 2.5x higher output speed at premium pricing
Several Claude models support an effort parameter that trades intelligence for latency and cost
Cache prompt prefixes with `cache_control` to cut costs and latency
